body: Cross-engine data point: same card, same model family, same day — llama.cpp b10335 with its draft-mtp speculative decoding (unsloth Q4_K_M GGUF, n-max 2 and 4) streamed the exact prompts that corrupted here **intact in every test** (3/3 on the quoted-sentence repro, temperature 0, thinking off). So the dropped-words behavior is specific to this stack's streamed-delta path under multi-token speculative steps, not to MTP-for-Qwen3.8 in general.

Recurrence with new arming evidence. We re-enabled MTP (n=2) today behind an automated streamed-vs-non-streamed diff canary, and the corruption was present **immediately on the first request after server start**:

```
STREAMED : The \\ a \-looking\, and it reflects the market's expectation of future price fluctuations...
NONSTREAM: The "implied" volatility is a "forward-looking" measure, and it reflects the market's expectation...
```

Same signature as the original report (quote-adjacent subwords dropped from stream deltas only). Combined with earlier observations, the arming model is now clear: **the defect arms (or not) per server boot** — three MTP restarts yesterday streamed clean under aggressive probing (cache-cold, concurrent, chunked-prefill races), while the original session and today's boot were corrupted on every streamed request from the first one. So a practical reproduction recipe: restart the server with MTP enabled and diff one streamed quoted sentence against its non-streamed twin; repeat restarts until armed (observed ~1 in 3-4 boots on our box). Config unchanged from the report (vLLM 0.27.1, unsloth Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, single Blackwell GPU). Happy to run an instrumented build across several boots — with the boot-level arming model, catching it live is now cheap.

Correction to the arming rate: it is not a per-boot coin flip. Today the corruption armed on **4 out of 4 consecutive MTP-enabled boots** (each caught within seconds by the diff canary and auto-disabled), while yesterday 3 out of 3 MTP boots on the same host streamed clean under aggressive probing. Identical unit config both days. So the arming looks bimodal by longer-lived host state rather than random per boot — the only notable host activity between the clean and armed days was running llama.cpp CUDA workloads on the same GPU between vLLM sessions. On its current state this host reproduces the corruption deterministically on every MTP boot, which makes it a reliable live-repro machine if an instrumented build would help.

Layer-by-layer audit of the v0.27.1 streaming path (source checkout, offline experiments — server untouched):

**Exonerated by direct testing:** `FastIncrementalDetokenizer` driven offline with the exact Qwen3.8 tokenizer and the exact corrupted sentence's token ids, in multi-token bursts (3/step and mixed 1-3-5/step mimicking accepted MTP drafts), with true prompt-ids priming — joined deltas == cumulative == expected text in every pattern. No loss.

**Verified sound by inspection:** `BaseIncrementalDetokenizer.get_next_output_text` offset accounting (advances exactly by what it returns); `RequestOutputCollector.put` + `RequestOutput.add` DELTA aggregation (concatenates text, appends unmatched indexes); the `stream_interval` gate (returns before any delta is consumed; default 1); single call-site for the delta getter (no second consumer). No `invalid prefix … resetting decode stream` warnings in the corrupted sessions' logs, so the DecodeStream reset/recovery path (#17448) did not fire.

**The constraint that survives everything:** in armed sessions, non-streaming responses are correct — and FINAL_ONLY returns the same `output_text` accumulated by the same `decode_next` calls — so token delivery and incremental decode are provably intact even while streamed delta chunks for whole subword spans never arrive at the client. The loss is strictly between completion-output emission and the wire, and only in the boot-armed state.

Next diagnostic we can run on the deterministic-repro host (needs one MTP boot): counter instrumentation at three points — deltas returned by `get_next_output_text`, chunks written by the serving layer, chunks received by the client — to pin which hop drops them. Happy to run a patch/branch if that instrumentation is useful to you.

## Root cause found: test-harness artifact, not a vLLM bug. Closing.

After a full audit of every observation in this issue, I can now show the "corruption" was produced by **my own SSE extraction pipeline**, not by vLLM. I'm closing this with an apology for the noise — details below so nobody else falls into the same trap.

### The harness bug

My quick-look probes (and a monitoring canary built from them) extracted streamed text with:

```sh
curl -N .../v1/chat/completions -d '{... "stream": true}' \
  | grep -ao '"content":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/^"content":"//;s/"$//' | tr -d '\n'
```

The regex `"content":"[^"]*"` terminates at the first `"` character — **including the `"` of an escaped quote (`\"`) inside the JSON string**. Any delta whose text contains an interior quote is silently truncated at that point, with everything after it dropped.

### Why it perfectly mimicked an MTP bug

Delta granularity is the confounder:

- **MTP off** → one token per SSE delta. Quote tokens arrive alone; word tokens arrive in their own quote-free deltas and survive extraction. Eyeballing the output, every word is present → "clean".
- **MTP on** → accepted speculative runs put several tokens in one delta, e.g. `"content":"The \"implied\" volatility"`. The regex truncates that delta to `The \` — whole words visibly vanish → "corrupted".

So the artifact tracked the MTP toggle exactly, and turning MTP off "fixed" it every time. The intermittent/per-boot pattern I reported was also illusory: sessions where I probed with a real JSON parser were "clean boots", sessions where I probed with the grep pipeline were "armed boots". The llama.cpp control was parsed with `json.loads` — which is why it looked clean.

### Verification that streaming is actually lossless

On the same build (v0.27.1, Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}`, FlashInfer, fp8 KV, Blackwell):

- Ran the two extraction methods against the **same streamed response**: the grep pipeline reproduces the exact "corruption" from my reports (`The \\ a \-looking\, ...`), while proper JSON parsing of the identical bytes yields the intact sentence.
- Instrumented `v1/engine/output_processor.py` (detokenizer delta production), `RequestOutputCollector` (aggregation), and the completions/chat serving generators (wire emission) with per-delta logging: across 3 separate boots, sequential + 8-way concurrent streamed requests, chat and raw `/v1/completions`, streamed text was **byte-identical to non-streamed** at every hop. No dropped deltas, no collector merges lost, no truncation.
- An ngram-spec-decode control (Qwen3-0.6B) on the same instrumented build: also lossless.

The earlier "layer audit" comment on this issue reached "all layers sound, loss must be between emission and the wire" — the correct resolution of that tension is that there was no loss at all.

Sorry for the churn, and thanks to anyone who spent time on this. Moral for fellow travelers: if a streaming bug's repro pipeline contains `grep -o '"content":"[^"]*"'`, suspect the pipeline first — speculative decoding changes delta granularity, which changes what that regex silently eats.
